name: Imatinib
summary: A small-molecule kinase inhibitor. It holds the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase, the abnormal enzyme made by the Philadelphia chromosome in chronic myeloid leukemia, in an inactive shape, so the growth signal it drives stops.

journey.title: Swallowed
journey.text: Imatinib is taken by mouth as a tablet.

journey.title: Dissolves
journey.text: The tablet dissolves and the drug moves on to the small intestine.

journey.title: Absorbed
journey.text: Imatinib crosses the intestinal wall into the portal blood. Absorption is nearly complete: mean absolute bioavailability of the capsule formulation is 98%.

journey.title: First pass through the liver
journey.text: Portal blood carries it through the liver before it reaches the general circulation. Little is lost on this pass, consistent with the 98% bioavailability.

journey.title: Carried in the blood
journey.text: About 95% is bound to plasma proteins, mostly albumin and α1-acid glycoprotein. Only the unbound fraction can leave the blood and enter cells.

journey.title: Reaches the leukemic cells
journey.text: In chronic myeloid leukemia the target cells are Philadelphia-chromosome-positive cells in the bone marrow and blood.

journey.title: Metabolised
journey.text: CYP3A4 is the main enzyme that metabolises imatinib. The main circulating metabolite, the N-desmethyl piperazine derivative, is also active. Half-lives are about 18 h for imatinib and 40 h for the metabolite.

journey.title: Eliminated, mostly in feces
journey.text: About 81% of a dose is eliminated within 7 days, 68% of it in feces (via bile), mostly as metabolites.

journey.title: and some in urine
journey.text: The remaining 13% of the dose that is eliminated in 7 days leaves in urine.

mechanism.title: Enters the cell
mechanism.text: Imatinib crosses the cell membrane to reach BCR-ABL, which sits in the cytoplasm.

mechanism.title: Locks the kinase shut
mechanism.text: It binds the ATP site of the ABL kinase domain while the kinase is in its inactive conformation, and holds it there.

mechanism.title: No phosphate is passed on
mechanism.text: With the site occupied, BCR-ABL cannot move phosphate from ATP onto its substrate proteins, so the growth signal it drives stops.

mechanism.title: The leukemic cell stops growing
mechanism.text: Without BCR-ABL signalling, BCR-ABL-positive cells stop proliferating and many undergo apoptosis (programmed cell death).

facts.label: Other kinases inhibited
facts.value: PDGF receptor and KIT (stem cell factor receptor)

simplified: Uptake into the cell is drawn as simple diffusion; transporters such as OCT-1 may contribute and their role is debated.
BCR-ABL drives several pathways (for example RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT and STAT5); they are drawn as one growth signal.
The body map is a schematic. Organ shapes and positions are approximate and not to scale.

sources.text: Gleevec (imatinib mesylate) tablets, US Prescribing Information, Novartis. Sections 12.1 Mechanism of Action and 12.3 Pharmacokinetics.
Schindler T, Bornmann W, Pellicena P, Miller WT, Clarkson B, Kuriyan J. Structural mechanism for STI-571 inhibition of Abelson tyrosine kinase. Science. 2000;289(5486):1938–1942.
